CHROMIUM: scripts: change dm_verity alg to sha256 Change dm_verity hash algorithm fom sha1 to sha256. Due to collision attacks against SHA1 and increasing severity of collisions there is a need to change the hash algorithm to SHA256. BUG=chromium:719966 TEST=Bootperf tool is used to make the boot performance measurements. Boot time measurements taken from kernel start to login screen from high performance/ low power ARM and x86 platforms show that changing dm_verity hash algorithm from SHA1 to SHA256 has boot time changes less than 277 ms on chrome_main when the crypto accelerators(for ARM) and SSSE3(for x86) kernel configurations are enabled. The difference is less for higher kernel versions and newer CPUs. For new kernel versions and CPUs the changes even increase boot time performance upto 717 ms.. Results are on go/cros-boot-sha256. Cq-Depend: chromium:1648858, chromium:1649075, chromium:1650153, chromium:1647547 Change-Id: I427415c5faf429c499471357ff3e8ffd314650a8 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1648943 Tested-by: Betul Soysal <betuls@google.com> Commit-Ready: Betul Soysal <betuls@google.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Alex Klein <saklein@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org>

Add a GetVideoParams call This allows XML-RPC clients to retrieve current video parameters, including the current detailed mode. The new GetVideoParams call returns a dict. Each field is optional because some video receivers don't support everything (e.g. VGA). The HDMI implementation is not populating the "clock" field because the HDMI receiver doesn't expose the transmitted pixel clock. The clock exposed by the receiver is the video output pixel clock, which is different. lakitu: Remove checking of uid and gid to be same Recently, when update engine tries to update an instance from old COS image to newer COS image, update gets failed. This happens due to following reason: 1. When google-account-daemon tries to allocate UID and GID for users that have existing /home/<user> dir, it tries to use old UID and GID if old UID and GID were same. 2. Recently, a new user 'crash' had been added with UID and GID as 20137. So, after the update, when google-accounts-daemon tries to allocate UID and GID for existing users, it is not able to use the old UID and GID as they are not same which is a mandate for the associated patch.Thereby, it assigns a new UID and GID which is greater than 20137 (above exisiting highest UID). This results in bad ownership while doing ssh as the UID and GID associated with /home/<user> is different from UID and GID of user. BUG=b:135045945 TEST=deleting user from /etc/passwd and /etc/group and trying ssh RELEASE_NOTE=None Change-Id: I01b69fd4cb9c51cd290ab17dd31a5e02ed4a65d2 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1668947 Tested-by: Vaibhav Rustagi <vaibhavrustagi@google.com> Commit-Ready: Vaibhav Rustagi <vaibhavrustagi@google.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Daniel Wang <wonderfly@google.com>
